subject: mass-communication
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
For the Optional Modules, attempt Module A (Traditional Media) or Module B (Photojournalism) in the sections that have both.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); the long answer 4 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Mass communication is 'public communication transmitted ______ or ______'.
State true or false: (i) Mass media have a strict code of conduct like doctors. (ii) Media can change people's attitudes and habits.
State true or false: (i) Traditional media are closest to people needing development messages. (ii) Comics should be created by outsiders.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – they should be created locally.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Define development communication.
questions.answer: The use of communication to promote development, i.e. to change or improve social and economic conditions of people.

questions.q: What are language newspapers?
questions.answer: Newspapers published in the different Indian languages; they are also called regional newspapers.

questions.q: What is a signature tune?
questions.answer: A piece of music specific to a programme, like the masthead of a magazine, played at the beginning.

questions.q: Differentiate between studio and outdoor recording.
questions.answer: Studio recording is within the four walls of a studio; outdoor recording is shooting outside it.

questions.q: Give any two examples of new media.
questions.answer: Websites and blogs (also social networking sites, online libraries, e-learning).

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What should be done while integrating traditional media with electronic media for development purposes? Write any two points of consideration.
questions.answer: Retain the social authenticity and original form of the traditional media; choose a suitable form for the region; keep collaboration between folk artists and producers.

questions.q: What is a ballad?
questions.answer: A poem usually set to music, often a story told as a song; used for messages on environment or dowry.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Who is a photojournalist? What is meant by wildlife photojournalism?
questions.answer: A photojournalist is a news photographer whose pictures support news stories; wildlife photojournalism photographs animals, needing advanced equipment and knowledge of animal behaviour and terrain.

questions.q: Name any two famous photojournalists of India with their work.
questions.answer: Raghu Rai – photographs of Indira Gandhi and Bhopal gas tragedy; Homai Vyarawalla – first woman photojournalist covering World War II.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Define mass communication and its process with 'channel of communication' using a flow diagram.
questions.answer: Mass communication is public communication transmitted electronically or mechanically. Process: Communicator (who) → Message (says what) → Channel (newspaper, radio, TV) → Receiver (to whom) → Effect (with what effect), with feedback from the receiver.

questions.q: Explain credibility, fairness and objectivity in news.
questions.answer: Cross-check facts; stay unbiased; hear both sides; credibility is the most important virtue because readers trust a paper for it.

questions.q: Explain why radio is called a medium that 'makes pictures'.
questions.answer: Listeners visualise scenes from sound, e.g. commentary on the Republic Day parade, using imagination.

questions.q: Explain how private channels emerged in India.
questions.answer: The Gulf War coverage by CNN led to satellite dishes and cable; STAR and an Indian company created Zee TV; the Supreme Court ruling of 1995 broke the government's monopoly of airwaves; regional channels followed.

questions.q: List three advertising principles and briefly describe them with examples.
questions.answer: Gain attention (size, colour, slogan); stimulate desire (make the product seem special or cool); impart conviction (show certainty, e.g. a fairness cream promising success).

questions.q: Discuss the impact of new media on interpersonal relations.
questions.answer: Youth chat online without meeting, so talking, listening and sharing skills and confidence suffer; balance and regulation of internet use are needed.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is meant by the 'inverted pyramid' method of writing? Explain in detail.
questions.answer: The most important facts come in the opening paragraphs; importance narrows down to the end; the least important details come last and can be cut without harming the story; it keeps the reader's interest and suits the lead.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write down any four advantages of traditional media that distinguish them from electronic media. Give examples.
questions.answer: Local and live with direct rapport (street play); flexible to new themes (tamasha); cost effective and need no special training (folk songs); immediate known feedback and emotional appeal.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of photographs in news reporting.
questions.answer: Photographs support written news with authority and emphasis, convey the news at a glance (a single picture is worth a thousand words), enhance the lead story, tell stories through photo essays and use composition for impact.
